skill.name: nature-writing
skill.description: Draft, restructure, or plan Nature-style manuscript sections from author-provided claims, results, figures, notes, or Chinese drafts. Use when the user wants to write or rebuild an abstract, introduction, related-work, method, experiments, discussion, conclusion, title, or full manuscript argument rather than only polish finished prose. Also trigger on general academic-writing requests even without the word "Nature", such as writing a paper from scratch, drafting a manuscript/section, structuring a paper, and Chinese phrasings like 学术写作、科研写作、论文写作、写论文、写paper、SCI写作、帮我写论文、搭论文框架、起草论文、写引言/摘要/讨论.
skill.summary: Plan and draft Nature-style manuscript sections from author-provided scientific claims, evidence, and notes.
skill.author: Community contribution, refactored into static/dynamic layers

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code spans, Mermaid diagrams, LaTeX equations, or academic writing guidance. I confirmed the fixed parent-directory references because the skill instructs agents to load shared files outside the packaged skill root. No prompt injection, malicious command execution, data exfiltration intent, or semantic abuse was found.

remediation.suggestion: Package shared files inside the skill or replace parent-directory references with skill-local paths. Avoid instructions that require reading outside the skill root.

content.value_statement: Researchers often have results and notes but lack a clear Nature-style manuscript argument. This skill turns supplied evidence into structured sections, outlines, and revision plans.
actual_capabilities: Routes requests by paper type, section, source language, and target journal.
Builds a one-sentence argument before drafting full prose.
Drafts abstracts, introductions, methods, experiments, discussions, conclusions, titles, and outlines.
Creates paragraph maps and terminology ledgers from supplied notes.
Adapts Chinese or mixed-language research notes into English scientific prose.
Flags missing claims, evidence, boundaries, and unsupported novelty.
limitations: Does not verify journal policies beyond bundled guidance.
Requires author-provided evidence; it should not invent results, statistics, references, or limitations.
May ask for confirmation before full drafting when framing is ambiguous.
Parent-directory shared references must be packaged correctly for reliable installation.

use_cases.title: Draft an introduction
use_cases.description: Turn claims, results, and gap notes into a paragraph map and Nature-style introduction draft.

use_cases.title: Adapt Chinese notes
use_cases.description: Convert Chinese or mixed-language lab notes into clear English manuscript prose with preserved scientific meaning.

use_cases.title: Review manuscript logic
use_cases.description: Check claim-evidence alignment, novelty boundaries, terminology consistency, and section structure before submission.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an abstract
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with notes and results.
prompt_templates.prompt:
Draft a Nature-style abstract from these notes. Use only the evidence I provide. First state the one-sentence argument, then draft the abstract.
[notes]

prompt_templates.title: Plan an introduction
prompt_templates.prompt:
Build an introduction outline for a Nature-family research article. Identify the gap, contribution, paragraph map, and missing evidence.
[topic, claim, results]

prompt_templates.title: Rebuild a method section
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request with an existing draft.
prompt_templates.prompt:
Rewrite this method section around module motivation, design, forward process, and verifiable advantages. Keep unsupported details as placeholders.
[section draft]

prompt_templates.title: Audit submission readiness
prompt_templates.prompt:
Run a rejection-risk self-review for this manuscript plan. Check claim-evidence alignment, novelty boundaries, experiment support, and terminology consistency.
[plan or draft]

output_examples.input: Notes for an abstract about a catalyst with measured conversion gains.
output_examples.output: A one-sentence argument, a 150-word abstract, and a list of missing evidence such as stability data and baseline details.

output_examples.input: A rough introduction that mixes background, method details, and results.
output_examples.output: A paragraph map that separates context, gap, approach, evidence, and significance, followed by a revised introduction draft.

output_examples.input: A method section for a three-module machine learning pipeline.
output_examples.output: A module-by-module structure with motivation, design, forward process, and evidence placeholders for each component.

best_practices: Provide core claim, evidence, and boundary before asking for full prose.
Review the one-sentence argument and paragraph map before expanding sections.
Mark uncertain data, missing comparisons, and invented wording for correction.
anti_patterns: Asking for a complete paper without supplying results or evidence.
Using the skill to create unsupported novelty claims.
Skipping confirmation when the target journal or section structure is unclear.

faq.question: Can it write a full manuscript from scratch?
faq.answer: It can plan and draft sections from supplied material. It should not invent results, methods, references, or claims.

faq.question: Does it support Chinese research notes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for adapting Chinese or mixed-language notes into English scientific prose.

faq.question: Which journals does it target?
faq.answer: It includes Nature, Nature-family, Nature Communications, and generic scientific manuscript guidance.

faq.question: Can it polish an existing English draft?
faq.answer: It can restructure and revise argument flow. Pure sentence-level polishing may fit a polishing skill better.

faq.question: Will it check factual accuracy?
faq.answer: It checks internal claim-evidence alignment, but it does not independently verify facts or citations.

faq.question: Why does it ask for confirmation?
faq.answer: The workflow pauses when the core claim, evidence, boundary, or journal framing is ambiguous.
